sentences.text: 3. This Court has perused and examined the impugned award as well as the materials and evidence available on record before the Tribunal.

4. The Tribunal under the impugned award has directed the appellant / Insurance Company to pay the 1st respondent / claimant a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- as compensation for the injuries sustained by him as a result of an accident caused by a vehicle insured with the appellant / Insurance Company.

The details of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the impugned award to the 1st respondent / claimant is as follows :-
 Heads Amount awarded  by the Tribunal  (Rs.)
 50% permanent disability (50 1,50,000  x 3000)
Medical bills 1,78,000  Transport and nutrition, 15,000  attender charges  Pain and sufferings 60,000  Loss of amenities and 60,000  enjoyment of life https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

Heads Amount awarded  by the Tribunal  (Rs.)
 Damages to clothing and 5,000  articles  Partial loss of income 32,000
The Tribunal has accepted the disability certificate issued by the Medical Board and has assessed the 1st respondent's disability at 50%.
The accident happened on 13.11.2016

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- towards the 50% permanent disability sustained by the 1st respondent / claimant as a result of the accident caused by a vehicle insured with the appellant.
The disability compensation was assessed by the Tribunal on percentage basis.

The Tribunal has assessed a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- at Rs.3,000/- per percentage of disability(i.e., 50 x 3000), which in the considered view of this Court cannot be found to be excessive as claimed by the appellant.

6. The Tribunal has also awarded a compensation of Rs.1,78,000/- towards reimbursement of medical bills of the 1st respondent / claimant incurred by him as a result of the injuries sustained by him, due to the accident caused by a vehicle insured with the appellant.
The sum of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Rs.1,78,000/- is supported by medical bills which have been marked as Ex.P8 before the Tribunal.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that a sum of Rs.1,78,000/- granted by the Tribunal towards medical bills is a just compensation.

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various other heads viz., transportation, nutrition,
attender charges, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities and enjoyment of life, damages to clothing and articles and partial loss of income as detailed supra, which in the considered view of this Court cannot be found to be excessive, considering the fact that the accident happened in the year 2016 and the 1st respondent / claimant had also sustained 50% disability.
Therefore, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is a just compensation and does not call for any interference by this Court.
8. However, the Tribunal has awarded an interest of 9%p.a. instead of 7.5% p.a, which is the settled practice, adopted by Tribunals all over the State of Tamil Nadu.
Therefore, the same has to be reduced by this Court.
Accordingly, the interest is modified from 9% p.a. to 7.5% p.a.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9
. In the result, there is no merit in this appeal.

However, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is disposed of by modifying the interest awarded by the Tribunal from 9%p.a. to 7.5% p.a. and in respect of other sums of money awarded by the Tribunal are concerned, the same remains unaltered.

10. The appellant / Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount awarded by the Tribunal along with interest @ 7.5% p.a., after deducting the amount already deposited if any, from the date of claim till the date of deposit and costs, to the credit of M.C.O.P.No.375 of 2017 on the file of the Special Subordinate Court, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Krishnagiri, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment.
